aggregates.note: the detector splits 3.5 at the decimal point and reports the fragment as 5 MILES. The declaration answers for the fragment the detector found, because a declaration that answers for a string the detector never saw is a declaration nobody checked.

the checkerboard scale bar's own end label, added in round two because a scale bar nobody can read the unit of is not a scale bar. It measures the SAME cable length the body of this slide already states, so it is the claim restated at the bar rather than a fresh assertion. The detector splits 3.5 at the decimal point and reports the fragment as 5 MILES; the declaration answers for the fragment the detector found.

the keepable frame's key for the instrument it draws, added in round two because the frame claimed a hero-scale staff and never named it. Same standing as the cover's axis key on slide 1: 59 is the whole window from the notice's publication (C20) to the filing deadline (C14) and 17 is today's position in it, which is a property of the DRAWING's calendar scale rather than a figure taken from the record.
the checkerboard scale bar's origin label, added in round three. It marks where the bar starts and measures nothing about the world; the bar's END label carries the claim.

the printed RATE for the filing sill's own axis, added in round three. It is a length on the drawing (155 design px at 3.1 px a day) and not an interval in the record; no event on this frame spans 50 days. It exists because the frame carries two axes both measured in days at rates 4.6x apart, and a reader given two rates has to be told them rather than left to infer one from the other.

the turbine row's own legend, added in round three. It states the drawing's glyph-to-object ratio, which is a property of the picture: 35 glyphs are drawn for the 330 to 350 turbines of C06, 33 full plus 2 half, so the row spans the range without inventing a midpoint. The same frame sets a one-to-one expectation 300 design px above it where 66 pods are 66 outlines, so leaving the ratio unstated invites a reader to count 35.
